2026-08-25T12:31:20.1953507Z <mcp-clis>
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1954047Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1954459Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1954810Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1955335Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1955760Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1956308Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1974600Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-25T12:31:20.1976650Z >
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2040698Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2043701Z >
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2044629Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2045500Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2045712Z ### How to Use
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2045971Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2046897Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2047702Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2047902Z ```bash
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2049553Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2050435Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2051110Z ```
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2051334Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2051635Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2052217Z ```bash
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2054053Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2054964Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2055893Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2056688Z ```
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2056924Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2057645Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2058822Z ```bash
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2059465Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2060200Z ```
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2060442Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2060808Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2061703Z ```bash
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2062296Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2063248Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2064011Z ```
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2064255Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2064564Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2065034Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2066562Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2068286Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2068702Z ```bash
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2069240Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2070177Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2071080Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2071439Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2071976Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2073091Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2073982Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2074522Z ```
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2074757Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2075589Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2076603Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2076807Z ```bash
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2077560Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2118944Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2120046Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2120572Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2121053Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2122007Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2122641Z ```
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2122882Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2123122Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2124122Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2125248Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2126352Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2127509Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2129043Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2129696Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2129895Z ### Notes
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2130151Z 
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2130844Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2132404Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2133760Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2135248Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2136568Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2137808Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2139065Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-25T12:31:20.2139830Z </mcp-clis>
